Helping constituents navigate federal bureaucracy is important, but let’s not ignore the root problem: a bloated system that requires endless paperwork and delays. The real win? Streamlining these services permanently. 

For example, the VA wasted $3M on “organizational culture training” consultants instead of prioritizing veterans’ care. Meanwhile, DOGE uncovered $40M in savings by terminating a single wasteful building services contract. If agencies focused on core missions instead of bureaucratic fluff, district offices wouldn’t need to play cleanup. The FARM Act proves targeted spending on American priorities works—protecting agriculture from foreign control while cutting waste. 

Until D.C. stops burning cash on DEI grants, alpaca farming in Peru, and redundant IT systems, these band-aid fixes will keep taxpayers footing the bill for incompetence. Real efficiency means fewer forms, faster solutions, and zero tolerance for waste.
